record.paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
record.original_question: Are the deformed power-law cosmological solutions of M-theory asymptotically stable, and does that stability support the naturalness of inflation in M-theory cosmology?

evidence.quote:
3.6 Stability of 11-dimensional supergravity cosmology II
Here the plan is to study the asymptotic stability of the deformed M-theory power-law cosmological solutions [65, 66]. This is especially important for the naturalness of inﬂation in M-theory cosmology.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider eleven-dimensional supergravity (the low-energy limit of M-theory) compactified on a product manifold M = M_{1+d} × K, where M_{1+d} carries a spatially flat FLRW metric

  ds^2_{1+d} = -dt^2 + a(t)^2 δ_{ij} dx^i dx^j,   i,j = 1,…,d,

and K is an internal manifold with time-dependent volume modulus b(t). The full eleven-dimensional metric is taken in the warped product form

  ds^2_{11} = -dt^2 + a(t)^2 dx_d^2 + b(t)^2 dy_{10-d}^2.

Augment the two-derivative supergravity action with the leading higher-derivative corrections (the quartic curvature R^4 terms together with their supersymmetric partners involving the three-form field strength) that arise as α'-type or κ^{2/3} corrections in M-theory. The resulting field equations admit "deformed power-law" cosmological solutions of the form

  a(t) = a_0 t^{p} (1 + δ_a(t)),   b(t) = b_0 t^{q} (1 + δ_b(t)),

where (p,q) is a power-law exponent pair determined by the corrected equations and δ_a, δ_b are deformations vanishing as t → ∞.

Questions:
(1) Are these deformed power-law solutions asymptotically stable under small homogeneous (and, more generally, inhomogeneous) perturbations of the metric and form-field moduli as t → ∞? Equivalently, do generic nearby initial data converge to a member of the deformed power-law family in the future?
(2) If so, does asymptotic stability of a member of the family with accelerating external scale factor (p > 1) hold on an open set of initial data large enough to make inflation in this M-theoretic cosmological setting natural, in the sense that it does not require fine-tuning of initial conditions?

Provide either a rigorous proof of asymptotic stability (with an explicit characterization of the basin of attraction) or a proof of instability.
artifact.status_search_result: A search for results on asymptotic stability of deformed power-law cosmological solutions arising from higher-derivative corrected eleven-dimensional supergravity / M-theory did not turn up a definitive proof of stability (or instability) of the relevant deformed power-law family, nor a rigorous result establishing naturalness of inflation in this M-theory setting. Related works address stability of power-law inflation in general relativity and modified gravity, but the specific M-theory question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Power-Law Inflation in Spacetimes Without Symmetry
status_evidence.snippet: Stability results for power-law inflation in general Einstein-scalar field cosmologies, without the higher-derivative M-theory corrections relevant to the problem at hand.
status_evidence.claim: Stability of power-law inflation is established in pure GR settings, but not in the deformed M-theory framework.

status_evidence.title: Stability in Cosmology, from Einstein to Inflation
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of stability questions in inflationary cosmology, discussing naturalness and basins of attraction.
status_evidence.claim: The general naturalness/stability problem for inflationary attractors remains a subject of active investigation.
